equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest (predominantly Stonepeak/Williams minority stakes in Louisiana LNG Infraco and Driftwood Pipeline, construction-stage)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 Annual Report Note E.8 / balance sheet, NCI book value $3,929m; deducted once here since flows are 100%-consolidated (see nci_treatment)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bottom-up production/price build, NOT a historical CAGR (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are dominated by the June-2022 BHP Petroleum merger (roughly doubling scale) and the FY2022 commodity-price spike (Brent/LNG at energy-crisis highs), making trailing 3yr and 5yr CAGRs on revenue, EPS and equity meaningless as forward growth proxies for this business -- FCF CAGRs are not computable at all because owner FCF is negative in the merger year context is unavailable pre-merger and negative in FY2025 (capex supercycle trough). Growth is instead built bottom-up from disclosed production additions (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) at a held-flat mid-cycle realized price (~$60/boe, in line with the FY2021/FY2023/FY2025 band excluding the FY2022 spike), per the mid-cycle commodity-price normalization approach specified for cyclical resources producers.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle commodity prices, on-schedule delivery of Scarborough (2026), Trion (2028) and Louisiana LNG (2029), stable 69-71% EBITDA margins, capex tapering to a ~19-20% sustaining level once the growth pipeline completes around FY2032.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structurally stronger LNG pricing on accelerated Asian coal-to-gas switching, full on-time/under-capital-intensity delivery of all three growth projects, and continued de-risking via strategic partner capital, supporting margin expansion toward 73% and a modest exit-multiple premium.
scenario_narratives.bear: A commodity downturn (echoing FY2020/FY2025 price troughs) combined with execution slippage or contracting shortfalls on Louisiana LNG (which lacks offtake for most volumes) and/or cost overruns on Scarborough/Trion, compressing margins to the low-60s% and keeping capex intensity elevated relative to a smaller revenue base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Woodside is valued as a commodity-price-geared oil & gas producer via an owner-FCF DCF built on mid-cycle (not trailing-CAGR) assumptions: realized price held near its stable ~$60-65/boe band (excluding the FY2022 energy-crisis spike) while volume growth is built bottom-up from three disclosed, substantially de-risked growth projects (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) already under construction and largely funded via committed partner capital (Stonepeak, Williams, LNG Japan, PEMEX). A 10-year explicit horizon is used because capex intensity and D&A are still normalizing from the current growth-capex peak toward a lower sustaining level well past year 5. The FY2025 reported free cash flow of -$782m is explicitly treated as a capex-cycle trough, not a valuation base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Concurrent execution risk across Scarborough, Trion and Louisiana LNG -- a delay or cost overrun on any one materially changes the capex and revenue-growth paths this model assumes

Louisiana LNG lacks offtake contracts for most of its volumes; a softer-than-modelled contracted price or a further required capital partner sell-down would compress both margin and Woodside's retained economic interest

Commodity price cyclicality dominates realized revenue even though EBITDA margin has been comparatively stable -- a sustained move below the ~$60/boe mid-cycle band (as in FY2020) would compress cash flow well below the base case regardless of production growth

The terminal value (8x cap multiple, 2.0% terminal growth, capturing ~depleting long-life reserves under an energy-transition backdrop) accounts for a large share of enterprise value typical of a resource producer; any structural acceleration of oil demand destruction would pressure this further out than the explicit horizon models

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement / remuneration note (share-based payments net of tax, US$70m); no separate equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (fully diluted weighted-average count used for EPS, FY2025 Annual Report note A.4)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-denominated flows (filings report US$m throughout) and a USD risk-free/ERP basis: rf ~4.2%, ERP ~5.0%, beta ~1.15 for a globally diversified but commodity-geared O&G major with investment-grade credit (Baa1/BBB+) -> cost of equity ~9.9%; blended with a modest debt weight at an after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% gives base WACC 8.5%. Risk (commodity cyclicality, project execution) is charged in the probability-weighted scenario flows per section 7f, not stacked again as a WACC premium; the same WACC is used across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): leases as debt. Lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows (reported FCF/OCF already reflects Woodside's own convention with lease payments in financing activities per IFRS 16); lease liabilities (US$1,759m at FY2025) are added to net debt alongside interest-bearing liabilities (US$11,963m), less cash (US$5,712m), matching the company's own published 'Net debt' gearing definition (Alternative Performance Measures note, FY2025 Annual Report: Net debt = interest-bearing liabilities + lease liabilities - cash = $8,010m). total_debt field above (13,722 = 11,963 + 1,759) is the interest-bearing-plus-lease gross figure consistent with that definition; net_debt = total_debt - cash = 8,010, tying to the filing.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated (100%) flows are used as the FCF base (reported_fcf, EBITDA, etc. are all as reported, pre-NCI). NCI is charged via a bridge deduction rather than attributable-only flows: FY2025 NonControllingInterest book value of US$3,929m (predominantly the Stonepeak 40% stake in Louisiana LNG Infraco and Williams' 10%/80% stakes in Louisiana LNG LLC/Driftwood Pipeline, both non-operating construction-stage entities as of FY2025; NCI was only US$754m a year earlier) is deducted in equity_bridge below. This avoids double-charging: the flows include 100% of Louisiana LNG capex/future revenue, and the bridge removes the minority claim on that value once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with commodity-cycle normalization, per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table (cyclical operating company -> owner-FCF DCF + owner-fcf-adaptations.md) and per the task brief. Woodside is a USD-reporting, AUD-quoted ASX oil & gas major; FX AUD/USD 0.702 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25), parity-checked against the WDS NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share): current_price x fx_rate ties to the ADR quote within 0.1%, confirming the rate and no ADR ratio adjustment needed (see data_sources.price for the live figures, which move on refresh). FY2025 reported FCF of -US$782m is a growth-capex-cycle trough (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG all under simultaneous construction), NOT distress -- do not read it as a base run-rate. EBITDA margin has in fact been stable-to-improving through the cycle (66.8%-71.4% FY2022-FY2025); nearly all of the earnings volatility is commodity PRICE (FY2025 realized price US$60.2/boe vs a FY2022 energy-crisis spike of US$98.4/boe, both against a stable 5-year band of ~US$60-69/boe ex-2022), not margin. Consequently the base-case revenue growth path is NOT a trailing-CAGR extrapolation (which would either double-count the 2022 price spike or extrapolate a price trough) -- it is built bottom-up from disclosed production growth catalysts at a held-flat, already-mid-cycle realized price: Scarborough (~8 Mtpa, 98% complete H1-2026, first cargo Q4 2026, full ramp through FY2027-28), Trion (Mexico oil, ~64% complete, first oil 2028, Woodside's ~$4.8bn net share), and Louisiana LNG (60% Woodside share of 16.5 Mtpa = ~9.9 Mtpa net, FID April 2025, ~28% complete H1-2026, first LNG 2029, ramping through the early 2030s). A 10-year explicit horizon is used because capex_pct and D&A_pct are still transitioning (elevated growth-capex cycle unwinding to a sustaining level) well past year 5, per section 2(d) of owner-fcf.md. Interest income (US$259m FY2025) is NOT stripped from FCF: Woodside carries net DEBT (US$8,010m per its own gearing definition), not net cash, so the interest-income-double-count rule (which applies only when net cash > 1x the FCF base) does not apply here; last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc = -782 - 70 = -852 (interest_income field held at 0 for this reason, not because none is earned). Cash tax rate is set at a normalized ~29% of EBIT (income tax + PRRT paid of $1,137m against an EBIT-proxy of $4,037m in FY2025 = 28.2%; underlying global EITR ~21.8-26.8% plus PRRT layering on top nets to a comparable ~28-30% cash rate), held roughly flat since PRRT/Australian company tax rates are structural, not cyclical. Balance-sheet anchors (net debt, shares, NCI) are FY2025 (2025-12-31), the latest annual filing extracted; no H1 2026 filing text was available in Extracted/ at build time, though the Analysis JSON's H1 2026 summary (FCF up >150% YoY to $352m, gearing still within the 10-20% target range, Scarborough 98% complete) is consistent with the trajectory modelled here and does not suggest the balance-sheet anchors are stale in a way that would move the valuation materially -- flagged for refresh once the FY2026 annual/H1 2026 half-year report is extracted.
inputs.fx_note: AUD/USD 0.702 at build (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25); refreshed to 0.702-equivalent alongside each price refresh. Parity-checked against the WDS NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share): AUD price x fx_rate ties the ADR quote within ~0.1%, confirming both the rate and direction (AUD*rate=USD) and that no ADR conversion ratio adjustment is needed.

bear.narrative: A global growth slowdown and/or OPEC+ supply response pushes Brent and Asian LNG benchmarks well below mid-cycle (echoing the FY2020/FY2025 downswings), compressing realized prices and margins even as production grows. Louisiana LNG, which still lacks offtake contracts for most of its volumes, faces further delay, a required additional sell-down (as flagged by S&P's negative outlook) or a softer contracted price; Scarborough or Trion experience cost overruns or schedule slippage typical of first-of-a-kind, multi-billion-dollar projects executed concurrently. Decarbonization policy and Australian approvals risk add friction to any further growth beyond the committed pipeline, and gearing runs persistently toward the top of or above the 10-20% target range, keeping capex intensity elevated relative to a smaller revenue base.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle Brent/LNG prices persist (~$60-65/boe realized, in line with the FY2021/23/25 band, excluding the FY2022 energy-crisis spike). Scarborough delivers first cargo on schedule (Q4 2026) and ramps through FY2027-28, Trion reaches first oil in 2028, and Louisiana LNG reaches first LNG in 2029 and ramps through the early 2030s -- all three projects complete broadly on the disclosed budgets and schedules, without major cost overruns or offtake shortfalls. EBITDA margin holds near its recent stable band (69-71%) as the new LNG trains add low-cost volume. Capex, elevated by the current three-project growth cycle (peaking near FY2025-26 levels), tapers to a ~19-20% sustaining level once Louisiana LNG is complete (~FY2032). Cash tax (company tax + PRRT) stays near its normalized ~29% rate.

bull.narrative: LNG demand tailwind runs hotter than the Wood Mackenzie base case (Asian coal-to-gas switching accelerates, additional supply delays elsewhere in the market keep prices firmer than mid-cycle at ~$65-70/boe realized). Scarborough, Trion and Louisiana LNG all deliver ahead of or on schedule with further partner sell-downs reducing capital intensity, Bass Strait operatorship synergies (>US$60m) materialize in full, and new long-term LNG offtake contracting (4.7+ Mtpa signed in 2025) continues at pace, supporting a modest exit-multiple premium and slightly lower WACC as credit-rating pressure eases.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 8x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because Woodside is running three very large, concurrent, first-of-a-kind capital projects (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) with disclosed execution risk (S&P negative outlook specifically tied to Louisiana LNG capex/portfolio risk) and Louisiana LNG in particular has not yet secured offtake for most of its planned volumes -- a real risk that the largest single growth driver undershoots. Combined with the business's inherent high commodity-price cyclicality (FY2025 NPAT fell 24% on a 14.4% Brent decline despite record volumes), the downside case is a plausible, not tail, outcome. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because it requires several largely independent things to go right simultaneously (pricing, all three projects, further capital-partner de-risking). Base gets the remaining 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
